text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) has been thrown into a quandry after its second choice parliamentary by-election contender was been transferred from Blantyre to Lilongwe more than 300 km away. MCP's first choice contender was at the 11th hour rejected by the Electoral Commission for not being a registered voter anywhere in Malawi.

- President Bakili Muluzi on Wednesday elevated Phalombe sub-boma in Mulanje to a full district making the total number of Malawi's districts 25. Mulanje and Phalombe have a total population of more than one million.

- President Bakili Muluzi on Wednesday lashed out at opposition parties who keep criticising his economic policies when prices are falling every day. "The prices of iron sheets have come down, so have those of bicyles, tubes and even soap," he told a rally at Phalombe.

- The National Compensation Tribunal said it has only paid out up to 15 percent of the official complaints lodged after government only provided 10 million kwacha of the 100 million the tribunal requested. Compensation claimants on Monday converged at the tribunal offices and threatened to demonstrate.
